stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

on the last line of your reply:

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "path": ".openclaw/tmp/continual_arc_notes.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC pattern note: center-2 ring on parallel 2 rails

Learned from solved task `task-1b58f78f` (3 demos; confirmed correct after submissions).

## Pattern
- Input has one or more 3x3 rings: eight `3`s around a center `2`. The center lies on a straight line/rail made of `2`s (the demos used vertical rails).
- For each ring, extend a full straight line of color `1` through its center, along the direction perpendicular to the rail (e.g. vertical rails => paint the entire center row horizontally with `1`). This fills all cells across the grid on that row except preserve the original ring's `3`s and center `2`.
- Where that beam crosses another parallel `2` rail, paint a 3x3 neighborhood centered on the crossing with `1`s, but preserve the crossing cell itself as `2`. Thus the two adjacent rows get 1s in the three columns centered on that rail; on beam row, the rail-center stays 2 while neighboring cells become 1. This may overwrite 2 rail cells in adjacent rows.
- Do not alter other cells. For the source ring crossing, its existing 3x3 ring remains unchanged; do not paint over its 3s or center 2.

## Evidence
- Demo with one vertical rail and one ring: full horizontal color-1 line through ring center, keeping ring intact.
- Demo with two vertical rails and two rings: each ring center row got the full horizontal beam; where a beam encountered the other rail, a 3x3 color-1 halo was added, retaining the center `2` at the crossing.
- Solved test had vertical rails at columns 2, 7, 11, 16 and rings centered at (row 2, col 2) and (row 12, col 11). Beams were rows 2 and 12; crossings with other rails got adjacent 3x3 patches, preserving each center crossing `2` on the beam row.

## Common pitfall
The intersection halo is exactly a 3x3 patch centered at the crossing, not merely a stripe along the beam; preserve the center rail's 2 on the beam row. The original source ring stays intact."
}
